title: Banking
verdict: Book frozen on stale prints — NPL 32.26%, CAR far below floor.

Tk12,000cr locked in interbank LC-guarantee disputes freezing trade-finance liquidity

runway.unit: bp of CAR buffer above the 10% floor

banker_read.verdict: On the Q1 2026 print NPLs sit at 32.26%, CAR 1.56% on the Q3 2025 read — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither refreshes until Q2 disclosure; the interbank system now carries Tk12,000cr locked in LC-guarantee litigation.

tldr: The book holds frozen — NPL 32.26% on Q1, CAR 844bp under the floor.
analysis: The banking book is frozen and the freeze is the story: NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 2026 read, system CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio) 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates the printed ratio. What moves is the forward vector, and it is broadening: RMG exports to the EU fell 16.4% in H1, thinning receivables, while Tk12,000cr sits locked in interbank LC-guarantee litigation — trade-finance disputes freezing liquidity at the plumbing level. Private credit at a 33-year-low 4.98% says weak sheets cannot out-grow their bad-loan stock. Dispersion stays the trade: own the private compounders, fade the SCB paper the resolution regime tests first.

title: Iran War & Oil
verdict: Brent breaks $90 — the paused relief reverses onto the import bill.

risk: Brent above $90 stacking crude plus freight onto a $1.77bn trade gap
The August cooking-gas hike compounding energy cost-push into the next CPI print

banker_read.verdict: Brent broke $90 to $90.74, WTI $84.44 — last week's relief has reversed, crude now $10.74 above the $80 FY27 assumption, not fading toward it. Each dollar re-widens the import bill and the fuel-subsidy claim; with the August cooking-gas hike booked, the energy cost-push compounds.

tldr: Brent breaks $90 to $90.74, now $10.74 above the FY27 line.
analysis: The relief is over: Brent broke $90 to $90.74 and WTI $84.44, reversing the fade that had parked crude below $90 for a week. That matters more for Bangladesh than the tape suggests. The country imports nearly all its fuel, so every dollar on Brent lands twice — first on the import bill a $1.77bn trade gap already strains, then on the FY27 fuel-subsidy provision built on an $80 assumption crude now sits $10.74 above. The timing compounds it: the August cooking-gas hike is already in train, so energy cost-push is rebuilding just as the CPI 12m-avg sits at 8.68% on the Jun print and private credit is dead at 4.98%. The oil break is the external counterweight to the demand-led calm holding the peg — watch H2 energy-importer receivables and the next subsidy claim. Treasury should price the reserve buffer, not the daily spot, as the real constraint.

chart_read.signal: Brent broke $90 to $90.74, WTI $84.44 — the spread near $6.30 — crude reversing last week's fade rather than fading to the $80 line.
chart_read.context: Up from $88.52 last print and now $10.74 above the $80 FY27 line — the first push through $90.
chart_read.implication: Treasury: each dollar on Brent re-widens the import bill and the FY27 subsidy claim — the $90 line has broken, watch $95.

banker_read.verdict: July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while the buffer stops rebuilding: reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo. Both hard-currency engines are soft as RMG-to-EU runs off 16.4%, and Brent's $90 break now pulls the other way on the import bill.

tldr: July remittance holds $2.82bn, a second straight month under $3bn.
analysis: The earned-dollar engine is idling and the wind has turned against it. July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn, flat across the window — and RMG exports to the EU fell 16.4% in H1: both hard-currency engines soft at once. What masks that is the demand side — USD/BDT firmed to 122.60 as importer dollar demand ebbed, a cooling economy with private credit dead at a 33-year-low 4.98% drawing fewer dollars than it earns. But calm built on weak imports is not calm built on strong inflows. Now the external side turns: Brent broke $90 to $90.74, re-widening an import bill soft demand had been narrowing, just as reserves sit at $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print with the August refresh overdue and remittance's margin over the $1.77bn trade gap near $1.05bn. The book stays long 122.60, positioned for the reserve refresh — not the daily spot — to set direction.

metrics.sub: July print — a second month under $3bn, flat all window
metrics.label: Monthly Remittance
